- Trackable clause edits for SOW Exhibit A (service definitions) and Exhibit D (billing).
- Clarity on acceptance criteria for the new batch pipeline (we note your standard acceptance section but want an explicit test plan and SLA carveout).
- Confirmation on data residency and audit logs post-change.

Attached: Cornerstone_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx, CS-4821_OrderForm_v3.pdf

Can your legal and pricing teams review and provide a consolidated redline + price impact by EOD Tuesday? We are on a tight procurement cadence.

Best,

Ben / Karthik / Alyssa — I reviewed Cornerstone's redlines. High-level legal notes (tracked in attached):

1) Exhibit A (SOW/service definitions)
- Accept the split of "Inference Tier B" into "Realtime B1" and "Batch B2" with condition that B2 capacity is explicitly described as best-effort for cold-started workloads. We will add a sentence limiting KB-cache persistence for B2 to avoid unlimited memory retention.

2) Exhibit D (Billing)
- The blended per-token + reserved throughput model is acceptable if we include a minimum monthly committed usage floor and an overage rate table. Cornerstone's proposed language to retroactively reprice prior months is not acceptable; suggest explicit effective date language.

3) Acceptance criteria / SLA
- We will provide an acceptance test plan for B2 (batch) tied to latency percentiles and throughput targets; however, SLA credits for B2 will be limited to 20% of those for B1 due to the workload profile. Need Cornerstone sign-off.

4) Data residency & audit logs
- We confirm we can keep logs in their region for production keys; will require a change of Project config on Redwood Private or Dedicated; scope this as implementation work.

I attached: Redwood_consolidated_redline_MSA.docx (redline) with inline comments and a short summary memo. A few specific asks for Cornerstone legal: remove proposed indefinite indemnity expansion (MSA §9.4) and accept our standard limitation of liability language with carveouts for willful misconduct.

Ben — I flagged problematic clauses and added suggested language. Karthik — please incorporate pricing impact comments and I'll call out legal-friendly phrasing in the Order Form.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Ben / Laura / Alyssa — pricing impact attached. Summary:

- Baseline (pre-change) estimated monthly bill: $42,900
- Proposed blended model (reserved 40% of capacity + per-token for burst/batch): estimated monthly bill: $48,700 (approx +13.4%).
- Key drivers: reserved throughput for realtime (B1) increases reserved spend; batch usages are highly spiky so per-token overage drives variability.

Recommendations:
- Move to a 6-month graded ramp for committed units (40% -> 60%) to reduce immediate sticker shock.
- Add a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration work (we suggest $8k credit applied first invoice).
- Provide explicit definitions for metering windows and example invoice calculations in Exhibit D to avoid disputes.

Attached: CS-4821_pricing_impact_v1.xlsx (cost workbook)

If Cornerstone agrees to the graded ramp and onboarding credit, net-first-year impact falls to ~+4% vs baseline. I'll incorporate Laura's legal phrasing into the Order Form lines and deliver a redlined Order Form for signature by 4/13 EOD, pending Ben's implementation checklist.

Karthik Iyer
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference
